title: JobBoard API
tagline: A Laravel 13 REST API with Sanctum auth, three-role RBAC, Redis caching, Docker, and CI/CD that deploys to AWS EC2 on every push.

links.docsNote: The live Swagger docs run on EC2, which is started and stopped on a schedule to save cost, so they may be offline at times.

highlights: Sanctum token authentication with custom RBAC middleware for Admin, Employer and Candidate
Redis caching on high-traffic endpoints; job listing filters by location, type, category and search
Tiered rate limiting: 5/min on auth routes, 60/min on the API
Dockerised MySQL, Redis and Apache; deployed to AWS EC2 with an Elastic IP
EventBridge starts and stops the instance on a schedule to cut hosting cost
GitHub Actions runs the test suite against MySQL and Redis services, then deploys over SSH

caseStudy.heading: Goal
body: Build a job board backend the way a production API would be built: token auth, role-based access, caching, rate limiting, automated tests, documentation, and a real deployment pipeline.

caseStudy.heading: Auth and access control
body: Laravel Sanctum issues API tokens. A custom role middleware guards route groups for Candidate, Employer and Admin, so each role can only reach its own endpoints. Employers can only change their own jobs, and candidates can only withdraw their own applications.

caseStudy.heading: Performance and abuse protection
body: High-traffic read endpoints are cached in Redis. Named rate limiters give auth routes a strict 5 requests per minute and the general API 60 per minute.

caseStudy.heading: Testing
body: 27 PHPUnit feature tests (57 assertions) cover authentication, RBAC, jobs and applications. CI runs them against real MySQL 8.0 and Redis service containers, not mocks.

caseStudy.heading: Delivery and cost
body: MySQL, Redis and Apache run in Docker Compose on an AWS EC2 instance with an Elastic IP. On every push to main, GitHub Actions runs the tests and, if they pass, deploys over SSH: pull, composer install, migrate and clear caches. An EventBridge schedule starts and stops the instance to keep hosting cost down.
